chunks: The exalted Shaykh Abu Ja'far Muhammad b. Ali b. al-Husayn b. Musa b. Babuwayh al-Qummi (ra) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. Ibrahim b. Ishaq (ra) narrated to us. He said: Ahmad b. Muhammad al-Hamadani, servant of Bani Hashim, narrated to us. He said: Ja'far b. Abdullah b. Ja'far b. Abdullah b. Ja'far b. Muhammad b. Ali b. Abi Talib narrated to us. He said: Kathir b. Ayyash al-Qattan narrated to us from Abu al-Jarud Ziyad b. al-Mundhir from Abu Ja'far Muhammad b. Ali al-Baqir (as). He said:

When Isa b. Maryam (as) was born, he was one day old as if he were two months old. When he was seven months old, his mother took him by the hand and came with him to the scribes and sat him in front of the teacher. The teacher said to him: Say: In the name of Allah, the Beneficent, the Merciful. So Isa (as) said: In the name of Allah, the Beneficent, the Merciful. The teacher said to him: Say the alphabet. So Isa (as) raised his head and said: Do you know what the alphabet is? So he raised a stick to discipline him, and he said: O teacher, do not discipline me. If you know, then well; otherwise, ask me so that I may explain it to you. He said: Explain it to me.

So Isa (as) said: Alif is the signs (alaa') of Allah, Ba is the delight (bahja) of Allah, Jim is the beauty (jamal) of Allah, and Dal is the religion (din) of Allah. Hawwaz: Ha is the horror (hawl) of Hell, Waw is the woe (wayl) of the people of the Fire, and Zay is the roar (zafir) of Hell. Hutti: the sins are dropped from those who seek forgiveness. Kalamun: the words (kalam) of Allah, for which there is no substitute. Sa'fas: a measure for a measure, and a reward for a reward. Qarashat: He gathers them and resurrects them. So the teacher said: O woman, take your son by the hand, for he is learned, and he has no need for a teacher.
ai.seo_question: What did Jesus explain about the Arabic alphabet according to Imam al-Baqir?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (as) narrates the story of the infant Jesus (as), who at seven months was taken by his mother Maryam to a teacher. When the teacher asked him to recite the Arabic alphabet (abjad), Jesus raised his head and asked whether the teacher knew its meaning. When the teacher moved to discipline him, Jesus stopped him and offered to explain, revealing that each letter group symbolizes divine attributes: A is the signs of Allah, B is His delight, J is His beauty, D is His religion, while H-W-Z represent the horrors of Hell, and subsequent letters represent forgiveness of sins, immutability of God's words, divine justice, and the final gathering of resurrection.

en.bilal-muhammad: Abu Ja`far Muhammad b. `Ali b. al-Husayn b. Musa b. Babuwayh al-Qummi (ra) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. Ibrahim b. Ishaq (ra) narrated to us. He said: Ahmad b. Muhammad al-Hamadani the servant of Bani Hashim narrated to us. He said: Ja`far b. `Abdullah b. Ja`far b. `Abdullah b. Ja`far b. Muhammad b. `Ali b. Abi Talib narrated to us. He said: Kathir b. `Ayash al-Qattan narrated to us from Abi’l Jarud Ziyad b. al-Mundhir from Abi Ja`far Muhammad b. `Ali al-Baqir (as). He said:

When `Isa b. Maryam (as) was born, he was one day old, but it was as though he was two months old. When he was seven months old, his mother took him by the hand to the scribes and sat him in front of the teacher. So, the teacher said: Say: In the name of Allah, the Beneficent, the Merciful. So, `Isa (as) said: In the name of Allah, the Beneficent, the Merciful. So, the teacher said: Say the alphabet. So, `Isa (as) raised his head and said: Do you know what the alphabet is? So, he took a stick to discipline him, so he said: O teacher! Do not discipline me. If you do not know, then ask me so that I may explain it to you. He said: Explain it to me.

So `Isa (as) said: “A” is the signs (alaa’) of Allah, “B” is the delight (bahja) of Allah, “J” is the beauty (jamal) of Allah, and “D” is the religion (din) of Allah. “H” is the horror (hawl) of Hell, “W” is the woe (wayl) of the people of the Fire, and “Z” is the roar (zafir) of Hellfire. “Ḥ” is the falling (hattat) of sins from those who repent. “K” is the words (kalam) of Allah, for which there is no substitute. “Sa`fas” is a measure (sa`) for a measure, and a reward for a reward. “Qarshat” means that He gathers them (qarashahum) and resurrects them. So, the teacher said: O woman! Take your son by the hand, for he is learned, and he has no need for a teacher.
